scenario: US Citizen, Permanent CA Resident, No Earned Income, Property Manager + Kalshi Trader, Income from Kalshi Futures + Rental + Savings Interest
core_answer: YES, you can absolutely fulfill the Medicaid/Medi-Cal work requirement with 0 earned income. The $580/month INCOME TEST is satisfied by ANY countable income source (unearned counts), not just earned income. Only ONE of the qualifying paths is needed EACH month you are checked (at least one month between 6-month renewals).

pathways.title: Path 1: Income Test ($580/month) — EASIEST for this user
pathways.how: Have gross monthly income >= $580 from any source (rental net + Kalshi net + interest combined count). For seasonal/irregular income (Kalshi trading is irregular), average >= $580 over prior 6 months counts.
pathways.counts: Rental net + Kalshi gains + interest + dividends + any other MAGI-countable income. DHCS: 'total gross income for a month must meet or exceed this amount' including unemployment benefits, SDI, retirement, dividends, etc.
pathways.difficulty: Low — passive income qualifies; no timesheet needed; verified via tax records/bank statements
pathways.example: If your rental net is $800/mo and interest $100/mo, you already meet threshold even with $0 earned and $0 Kalshi that month. If Kalshi is your only income and you had $5,000 gain in Jan but $0 in Feb-Apr, your 6-month average may still exceed $580.

pathways.title: Path 2: Self-Employment Work (Property Manager)
pathways.how: Document property management as self-employment (Schedule C). 80 hrs/month of self-employment hours satisfies requirement AND income from it also counts toward income test.
pathways.counts: If you materially participate and spend time managing properties, log hours. Even part-time management fees (e.g., 10% of rent collected) are self-employment earned income.
pathways.difficulty: Medium — need to demonstrate business activity, keep logs, file Schedule C; SE tax applies if net >=$400
pathways.example: Manage 5 units, show 20 hrs/week of showings, leasing, maintenance coordination = ~80 hrs/month. File Schedule C for management fees.
pathways.flag: If your rental activity is purely passive ownership (no management services), it is unearned rental income on Schedule E, not Schedule C earned work hours. Only counts for income test (P1), not work hours, unless you can document active property management as a business.

pathways.title: Path 3: Community Service / Volunteering (80 hrs/month)
pathways.how: Volunteer or do community service >=80 hrs/month (or combine with other activities). No income needed. California will maintain list of available opportunities per MEDIL I26-25.
pathways.counts: Any qualified community service organization; DHCS to publish local resource list.
pathways.difficulty: High — 20 hrs/week unpaid time commitment; documentation burden every 6 months; risk of administrative loss if paperwork missed

pathways.title: Path 4: Education (Half-Time Enrollment)
pathways.how: Enroll at least half-time in an educational program, career/technical education, GED/HSE, or work program. Half-time = about 6 credit hours/term for college.
pathways.counts: Enrollment alone satisfies requirement regardless of grades; less-than-half-time can combine hours with work/volunteering to reach 80.
pathways.difficulty: Medium — tuition costs unless free community college/training; enrollment verification required

pathways.title: Path 5: Work Program (80 hrs/month)
pathways.how: Participate in approved job training, workforce development, or career coaching program >=80 hrs/month. Includes on-the-job training, entrepreneurship programs.
pathways.counts: State-approved work programs; EDD workforce programs may qualify.
pathways.difficulty: Medium — must find qualifying program; California to publish list

pathways.title: Path 6: Exemption (No Requirement at All)
pathways.how: Qualify for mandatory exemption: medically frail/special medical needs (must be clinically determined), parent/caregiver of child <=13 or disabled individual, disability determination (Aged/Blind/Disabled Medi-Cal group), TANF/SNAP compliance, Medicare, American Indian/Alaska Native, etc. Exempt individuals also stay on ANNUAL renewals (not 6-month).
pathways.counts: If exempt, no hours or income test needed at all.
pathways.difficulty: Only if legitimately qualifying — requires medical or other documentation; not a strategy for healthy adults without qualifying status

pathways.title: Path 7: Short-Term Hardship Exemption (California-Specific)
pathways.how: California has opted to grant ALL optional hardship exemptions: reside in county with federally declared disaster/emergency; reside in county with high unemployment; inpatient hospital/SNF/nursing facility stay; related outpatient care; medical travel for complex condition.
pathways.counts: Automatically applied by state for disaster/unemployment based on residence; must request for medical/hospitalization.
pathways.difficulty: Situational only — not a permanent compliance strategy, but useful for gaps

recommendation_for_user: For this user's profile (healthy adult, no children under 13 described, income from passive sources + active Kalshi trading): BEST PATH is P1 Income Test. You do NOT need earned income. Your combined net rental + net Kalshi gains + interest easily exceed $580 in most months; if trading is seasonal, the 6-month averaging rule protects you. KEEP RECORDS: bank statements showing deposits, Schedule E (rental), Schedule D/6781 (Kalshi), 1099-INT. At each 6-month renewal, state will check ex parte via FTB/tax data first; only if not found will they ask you. Fallback: P3/P4 if income dips to zero for 6 straight months (rare if you have rental). Document everything 30 days after notice if asked.
